MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  APRIL 15, 2025

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  An adjourned meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills
  Estates was called to order at 6:01 p.m. at City of Rolling Hills Estates Council Chamber,
  4045 Palos Verdes Dr. N., Rolling Hills Estates, California, by CHAIR PERSICHINA.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  CHAIR PERSICHINA led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Persichina, Pope, Ciarolla, Holdsworth, Bain,
  and McCormick

  Commissioners Absent:  Johnson

  City Staff Present:  Community Development Director Jeannie
  Naughton
  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Community Services Coordinator Matt Morrow

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING DRAFT MINUTES OF
  FEBRUARY 18, 2025

  COMMISSIONER BAIN made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  HOLDSWORTH to:

  APPROVE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  FEBRUARY 18, 2025.

  There being no objection, CHAIR PERSICHINA so ordered.

  B.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING DRAFT MINUTES OF MARCH
  18, 2025

  COMMISSIONER BAIN made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR POPE to:

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  1
April 15, 2025
   APPROVE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  MARCH 18, 2025.

  There being no objection, CHAIR PERSICHINA so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  NONE.

  6.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  REVIEW OF STREET TREES FOR 927 DEEP VALLEY DRIVE PROJECT

  Director Naughton gave a brief overview of the street trees for 927 Deep Valley
  Drive project (as per the agenda materials).

  COMMISSIONER BAIN inquired who would be responsible for the tree trimming.
  Superintendent Goldsmith stated that the City would be responsible as the trees
  are in a City right-of-way.

  Superintendent Goldsmith stated that he did not foresee an issue regarding the
  City tree maintenance budget and the future maintenance of the additional trees
  included in this project, in response to COMMISSIONER BAIN.

  VICE CHAIR POPE made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  MCCORMICK to:

  APPROVE THE PROPOSED RIGHT-OF-WAY LANDSCAPE
  IMPROVEMENTS FOR 927 DEEP VALLEY DRIVE.

  There being no objection, CHAIR PERSICHINA so ordered.

  B.  MILITARY SERVICE MEMBER BANNER PROGRAM PROPOSAL

  Supervisor Pinuelas gave a brief overview of the military service member banner
  program proposal (as per the agenda material).

  Supervisor Pinuelas confirmed that the proposed would replace the standard
  theme of the current banner program during 2026, in response to VICE CHAIR
  POPE.

  In response to CHAIR PERSICHINA, Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the vendor
  provides a minimum of twenty-five banners but based on light pole availability there
  could be a maximum of approximately forty-six banners.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  2
April 15, 2025
   In response to VICE CHAIR POPE, Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the entire
  program is paid by sponsorships with no additional contributions from the City. She
  also stated that the vendor would manage the program and that the sponsoring
  organizations would have a business logo or name on the banner.

  VICE CHAIR POPE commended Staff on finding a way to bring this program to
  the City.

  COMMISSIONER HOLDSWORTH asked if the vendor used a screening process
  for the photos and names submitted. Supervisor Pinuelas stated that Staff would
  confirm that with the vendor.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN requested that the Commission be shown banner designs
  prior to the finalization of the program.

  COMMISSIONER HOLDSWORTH made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR
  POPE to:

  RECOMMEND TO CITY COUNCIL TO APPROVE THE CGI
  COMMUNITY SHOWCASE BANNER PROGRAM’S 2026 THEME TO
  CELEBRATE MILITARY SERVICE MEMBERS AND THE 250TH
  ANNIVERSARY OF THE DECLARATION OF INDEPENDENCE.

  There being no objection, CHAIR PERSICHINA so ordered.

  7.  STAFF ITEMS

  A.  PETER WEBER EQUESTRIAN CENTER HAYRIDES UPDATE (VERBAL
  REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas gave a brief overview of the Peter Weber Equestrian Center
  regaining access to the Palos Verdes Landfill site for their hayrides to resume.

  In response to COMMISSIONER BAIN, Supervisor Pinuelas stated that there
  appeared to be a misunderstanding with new Los Angeles County Sanitation
  Districts staff regarding the Peter Weber Equestrian Center’s previously approved
  access to the public loop and maintenance roads inside the PV Landfill for their
  hayrides.

  B.  MAYOR’S RIDE UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Coordinator Morrow gave a brief update on the Mayor’s Breakfast Ride event. He
  went over the details regarding the horse ride portion of the event as well as some
  updates regarding the Scout’s Breakfast portion of the event at Ernie Howlett Park.

  C.  HILLS ARE ALIVE UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  3
April 15, 2025
   Coordinator Morrow gave a brief update on the upcoming Hills Are Alive 5k/10k
  event. He updated the Commission regarding event sponsorships, registration,
  and marketing.

  D.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE.
  8.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE.

  B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE.

  9.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF MARCH 25, 2025

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF APRIL 8, 2025

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  10.  PARK TOURS

  A.  CHANDLER PARK, PEPPERWOOD PARK, ROCKBLUFF PARK, AND SILVER
  SPUR PARK

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the Commission would only be touring Chandler
  Park and Pepperwood Park as there was nothing of notable interest at Rockbluff
  Park and Silver Spur Park for the Commission that was not listed in the agenda
  materials.

  **AT THIS POINT THE COMMISSION WALKED TO CHANDLER PARK FOR A
  TOUR**

  Superintendent Goldsmith noted that the City’s maintenance of the gopher control
  at the park had improved from the previous year. He also noted that the
  replacement of the perimeter fencing is ongoing and the new fencing will be vinyl
  instead of wood.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  4
April 15, 2025
   In response to COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK, Staff indicated that Chandler Park
  does continue to be a park that has small use from the public.

  Superintendent Goldsmith shared that the park lost three trees due to a tree fungus
  that affects California Pepper trees. He stated that there are plans to replace the
  trees.

  **AT THIS POINT THE COMMISSION WALKED TO PEPPERWOOD PARK FOR
  A TOUR**

  Superintendent Goldsmith stated that a Juniper tree had to be removed from the
  right of way adjacent to the park and that two California Pepper trees would be
  installed to replace the Juniper tree. Supervisor Pinuelas shared that the two
  California Pepper trees were donated by Bennett Landscape for Arbor Day.

  11.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR PERSICHINA ADJOURNED THE MEETING AT 6:41 PM TO THE NEXT
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING ON MAY 20, 2025, AT 6:00
  P.M., WHICH WILL BE HELD AT GEORGE F CANYON NATURE CENTER.

  There being no objection, so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  __________________________
  Matt Morrow  Lou Persichina
  Community Services Coordinator  Chair, Park & Activities Commission

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  5
April 15, 2025
